verses.zh: 奉　神旨意，蒙召作耶稣基督使徒的保罗，同兄弟所提尼，
verses.en: From Paul,[NOTE:1] called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus[NOTE:2] by the will of God, and Sosthenes, our brother,
notes: Grk “Paul.” The word “From” is not in the Greek text, but has been supplied to indicate the sender of the letter.

Many significant mss, as well as several others (א A Ψ 1739 1881 M sy), have a reversed order of these words and read “Jesus Christ” rather than “Christ Jesus” (P46 B D F G 33 it). The meaning is not affected in either case, but the reading “Christ Jesus” is preferred both because it has somewhat better attestation and because it is slightly more difficult and thus more likely the earlier reading (a scribe who found it would be prone to change it to the more common expression). At the same time, Paul is fond of the order “Christ Jesus.” As well, the later Pauline letters almost uniformly use this order in the salutations. Thus, on both external and internal grounds, “Christ Jesus” is the preferred reading here.

verses.zh: 写信给在哥林多　神的教会，就是在基督耶稣里成圣、蒙召作圣徒的，以及所有在各处求告我主耶稣基督之名的人。基督是他们的主，也是我们的主。
verses.en: to the church of God that is in Corinth,[NOTE:1] to those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, and called to be saints, with all those in every place who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see JP1-C2; JP2-C2; JP3-C2; JP4-C2.
Grk “theirs and ours.”

verses.zh: 愿恩惠、平安从　神我们的父并主耶稣基督归与你们。
verses.en: Grace and peace to you[NOTE:1] from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ!
notes: Grk “Grace to you and peace.”

verses.zh: 我常为你们感谢我的　神，因　神在基督耶稣里所赐给你们的恩惠；
verses.en: I always thank my God for you because of the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus.

verses.zh: 又因你们在他里面凡事富足，口才、知识都全备，
verses.en: For you were made rich[NOTE:1] in every way in him, in all your speech and in every kind of knowledge[NOTE:2]—
notes: Made rich refers to how God richly blessed the Corinthians with an abundance of spiritual gifts (cf. v. 7).

Speech and knowledge refer to the spiritual gifts God had blessed them with (as v. 7 confirms). Paul will discuss certain abuses of their gifts in chapters 12-14, but he thanks God for their giftedness.

verses.zh: 正如我为基督作的见证，在你们心里得以坚固，
verses.en: just as the testimony about Christ has been confirmed among you—

verses.zh: 以致你们在恩赐上没有一样不及人的，等候我们的主耶稣基督显现。
verses.en: so that you do not lack any spiritual gift as you wait for the revelation[NOTE:1] of our Lord Jesus Christ.
notes: The revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ refers to the Lord’s return, when he will be revealed (cf. the reference to the day of our Lord Jesus Christ in v. 8).

verses.zh: 他也必坚固你们到底，叫你们在我们主耶稣基督的日子无可责备。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] will also strengthen you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
notes: Grk “who,” referring to Christ. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.

verses.zh: 神是信实的，你们原是被他所召，好与他儿子―我们的主耶稣基督一同得分。
verses.en: God is faithful, by whom you were called into fellowship with his son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.zh: 弟兄们，我藉我们主耶稣基督的名劝你们都说一样的话。你们中间也不可分党，只要一心一意，彼此相合。
verses.en: I urge you, brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to agree together,[NOTE:2] to end your divisions,[NOTE:3] and to be united by the same mind and purpose.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “brothers,” but the Greek word may be used for “brothers and sisters” or “fellow Christians” as here (cf. BDAG 18 s.v. ἀδελφός 1, where considerable nonbiblical evidence for the plural ἀδελφοί [adelphoi] meaning “brothers and sisters” is cited).
Grk “that you all say the same thing.”
Grk “that there be no divisions among you.”
Grk “that you be united in/by the same mind and in/by the same purpose.”

verses.zh: 因为革来氏家里的人曾对我提起弟兄们来，说你们中间有纷争。
verses.en: For members of Chloe’s household have made it clear to me, my brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] that there are quarrels[NOTE:2] among you.
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:10.
Or “rivalries, disputes.”

verses.zh: 我的意思就是你们各人说：「我是属保罗的」；「我是属亚波罗的」；「我是属矶法的」；「我是属基督的」。
verses.en: Now I mean this, that[NOTE:1] each of you is saying, “I am with Paul,” or “I am with Apollos,” or “I am with Cephas,”[NOTE:2] or “I am with Christ.”
notes: Or “And I say this because.”
Cephas. This individual is generally identified with the Apostle Peter (L&N 93.211). Both the Aramaic name “Cephas” and the Greek name “Peter” are related to words in each language which mean “rock.”

verses.zh: 基督是分开的吗？保罗为你们钉了十字架吗？你们是奉保罗的名受了洗吗？
verses.en: Is Christ divided? Paul wasn’t crucified for you, was he?[NOTE:1] Or were you in fact baptized in the name of Paul?[NOTE:2]
notes: Questions prefaced with μή (mē) in Greek anticipate a negative answer. This can sometimes be indicated by using a “tag” at the end in English (here the tag is “was he?”).

This third question marks a peak in which Paul’s incredulity at the Corinthians’ attitude is in focus. The words “in fact” have been supplied in the translation to make this rhetorical juncture clear.

verses.zh: 我感谢　神，除了基利司布并该犹以外，我没有给你们一个人施洗，
verses.en: I thank God[NOTE:1] that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,
notes: The oldest and most significant witnesses to this text, as well as a few others (א* B 6 1739 sams bopt), lack the words τῷ θεῷ (tō theō, “God”), while the rest have them. An accidental omission could well account for the shorter reading, especially since θεῷ would have been written as a nomen sacrum (eucaristwtwqMw). However, one might expect to see, in some mss at least, a dropping of the article but not the divine name. Internally, the Pauline introductory thanksgivings elsewhere always include τῷ θεῷ after εὐχαριστῶ (eucharistō, “I thank”; cf. Rom 1:8; 1 Cor 1:4; Phil 1:3; Phlm 4; in the plural, note Col 1:3; 1 Thess 1:2). However, both the fact that this is already used in 1 Cor 1:4 (thus perhaps motivating scribes to add it ten verses later), and that in later portions of his letters Paul does not consistently use the collocation of εὐχαριστῶ with τῷ θεῷ (Rom 16:4; 1 Cor 10:30), might give one pause. Still, nowhere else in the corpus Paulinum do we see a sentence begin with εὐχαριστῶ without an accompanying τῷ θεῷ. A decision is difficult, but on balance it is probably best to retain the words.

verses.zh: 免得有人说，你们是奉我的名受洗。
verses.en: so that no one can say that you were baptized in my name!

verses.zh: 我也给司提法那家施过洗，此外给别人施洗没有，我却记不清。
verses.en: (I also baptized the household of Stephanus. Otherwise, I do not remember whether I baptized anyone else.)

verses.zh: 基督差遣我，原不是为施洗，乃是为传福音，并不用智慧的言语，免得基督的十字架落了空。
verses.en: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel—and not with clever speech, so that the cross of Christ would not become useless.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “would not be emptied.”

verses.zh: 因为十字架的道理，在那灭亡的人为愚拙；在我们得救的人，却为　神的大能。
verses.en: For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

verses.zh: 就如经上所记：我要灭绝智慧人的智慧，废弃聪明人的聪明。
verses.en: For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will thwart the cleverness of the intelligent.”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Isa 29:14.

verses.zh: 智慧人在哪里？文士在哪里？这世上的辩士在哪里？　神岂不是叫这世上的智慧变成愚拙吗？
verses.en: Where is the wise man? Where is the expert in the Mosaic law?[NOTE:1] Where is the debater of this age? Has God not made the wisdom of the world foolish?
notes: Grk “the scribe.” The traditional rendering of γραμματεύς (grammateus) as “scribe” does not communicate much to the modern English reader, for whom the term might mean “professional copyist,” if it means anything at all. The people referred to here were recognized experts in the law of Moses and in traditional laws and regulations. Thus “expert in the Mosaic law” comes closer to the meaning for the modern reader.

verses.zh: 世人凭自己的智慧，既不认识　神，　神就乐意用人所当作愚拙的道理拯救那些信的人；这就是　神的智慧了。
verses.en: For since in the wisdom of God the world by its wisdom did not know God, God was pleased to save those who believe by the foolishness of preaching.

verses.zh: 犹太人是要神迹，希腊人是求智慧，
verses.en: For Jews demand miraculous signs and Greeks ask for wisdom,

verses.zh: 我们却是传钉十字架的基督，在犹太人为绊脚石，在外邦人为愚拙；
verses.en: but we preach about a crucified Christ,[NOTE:1] a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles.
notes: Or “Messiah”; Grk “preach Christ [Messiah] crucified,” giving the content of the message.

verses.zh: 但在那蒙召的，无论是犹太人、希腊人，基督总为　神的能力，　神的智慧。
verses.en: But to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.

verses.zh: 因　神的愚拙总比人智慧，　神的软弱总比人强壮。
verses.en: For the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom,[NOTE:1] and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “than men.”
Grk “than men.”

verses.zh: 弟兄们哪，可见你们蒙召的，按着肉体有智慧的不多，有能力的不多，有尊贵的也不多。
verses.en: Think about the circumstances of your call,[NOTE:1] brothers and sisters.[NOTE:2] Not many were wise by human standards,[NOTE:3] not many were powerful, not many were born to a privileged position.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “Think about your calling.” “Calling” in Paul’s writings usually refers to God’s work of drawing people to faith in Christ. The following verses show that “calling” here stands by metonymy for their circumstances when they became Christians, leading to the translation “the circumstances of your call.”
Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:10.
Grk “according to the flesh.”
The Greek word ευγενής (eugenēs) refers to the status of being born into nobility, wealth, or power with an emphasis on the privileges and benefits that come with that position.

verses.zh: 神却拣选了世上愚拙的，叫有智慧的羞愧；又拣选了世上软弱的，叫那强壮的羞愧。
verses.en: But God chose what the world thinks foolish to shame the wise, and God chose what the world thinks weak to shame the strong.

verses.zh: 神也拣选了世上卑贱的，被人厌恶的，以及那无有的，为要废掉那有的，
verses.en: God chose[NOTE:1] what is low and despised in the world, what is regarded as nothing, to set aside what is regarded as something,
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

verses.zh: 使一切有血气的，在　神面前一个也不能自夸。
verses.en: so that no one can boast in his presence.

verses.zh: 但你们得在基督耶稣里是本乎　神，　神又使他成为我们的智慧、公义、圣洁、救赎。
verses.en: He is the reason you have a relationship with Christ Jesus,[NOTE:1] who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption,
notes: Grk “of him you are in Christ Jesus.”

verses.zh: 如经上所记：「夸口的，当指着主夸口。」
verses.en: so that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Jer 9:24. The themes of Jer 9 have influenced Paul’s presentation in vv. 26-31. Jeremiah calls upon the wise, the strong, and the wealthy not to trust in their resources but in their knowledge of the true God—and so to boast in the Lord. Paul addresses the same three areas of human pride.

Every paragraph has one central topic, truth, or thought. Each version encapsulates that topic in its own distinct way. WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 1 CORINTHIANS 1:1

1Paul, called as an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,

1:1 "Paul" Most Jews of Paul's day living outside of Palestine had two first names, one Jewish and one Roman
(cf. Acts 13:9). Paul's Jewish name was Saul. He, like the ancient King of Israel, was of the tribe of Benjamin
(cf. Rom. 11:1; Phil. 3:5). His Roman or Greek name, Paul, meant "little." This referred either

- to his physical stature, which was alluded to in a second century non-canonical book, The Acts
of Paul, in a chapter related to Thessalonica called "Paul and Thecla"

- to his personal sense of being the least of the saints because he originally persecuted the
Church (cf. 1 Cor. 15:9; Eph. 3:8; 1 Tim. 1:15)

- simply to the name given by his parents at birth

▣ "called" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED

▣ "an apostle" This is a common Greek word for "send" (i.e., apostellō). This term developed several theological usages.

- Greek literature and the rabbis used it as one called and sent as an official representative of another, something
like our English "ambassador" (cf. 2 Cor. 5:20).

- The Synoptic Gospels often use this term of Jesus being sent by the Father (cf. Matt. 10:40; 15:24; Mark 9:37;
Luke 9:48).

- In John the term takes on Messianic overtones (cf. John 4:34; 5:24,30,36,37,38;
6:29,38,39,40,57; 7:29; 8:42; 10:36; 11:42; 17:3,8,18,21,23,25; 20:21).

- It is used of Jesus sending believers (cf. John 17:18; 20:21).

- In the NT it is used for disciples.

- the original Twelve who were an inner circle of disciples (cf. Luke 6:13; Acts 1:21-22)

- a special group of Apostolic helpers and co-workers

(1) Barnabas (cf. Acts 14:4,14)

(2) Andronicus and Junias (KJV, Junia, cf. Rom. 16:7)

(3) Apollos (cf. 1 Cor. 4:6-9)

(4) James, the Lord's brother (cf. Gal. 1:19)

(5) Silvanus and Timothy (cf. 1 Thess. 2:6)

(6) possibly Titus (cf. 2 Cor. 8:23)

(7) possibly Epaphroditus (cf. Phil. 2:25)

- an ongoing gift in the church (cf. 1 Cor. 12:28-29; Eph. 4:11)

- Paul uses this title for himself in most of his letters as a way of asserting his God-given call
and authority as Christ's representative (cf. Rom. 1:1; 1 Cor. 1:1; 2 Cor. 1:1; Gal. 1:1; Eph. 1:1;
Col. 1:1; 1 Tim. 1:1; 2 Tim. 1:1; Titus 1:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEND

▣ "Jesus Christ" These terms are part of the fuller title, "the Lord Jesus Christ" (cf. 1 Cor. 1:2,3,7,8,9,10). These
three titles all have individual theological significance.

- "Jesus" is the name given to the baby in Bethlehem by the angel (cf. Matt. 1:21). It is made up of two Hebrew
nouns: "YHWH," the covenant name for Deity, and "salvation" (i.e., Hosea). It is the Aramaic form of the Hebrew
name Joshua. When used alone it often identifies the man, Jesus of Nazareth, son of Mary (e.g., Matt. 1:16,25;
2:1; 3:13,15,16).

- "Christ" is the Greek translation of the Hebrew Messiah (i.e., an Anointed One). It asserts Jesus' OT
title as YHWH's promised One sent to set up the new age of righteousness.

- "Lord" (used in 1 Cor. 1:1 in KJV) is the translation of the Hebrew term adon, which meant "owner,
husband, master, or lord." The Jews became afraid of pronouncing the sacred name YHWH lest they take it in
vain and break one of the Ten Commandments. Whenever they read the Scriptures, they substituted Adon
for YHWH. This is why our English translations use all capitals Lord for YHWH
in the OT. By transferring this title (kurios in Greek) to Jesus, the NT authors assert His Deity
and equality with the Father.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (adon and kurios)

▣ "by the will of God" This is the first of several emphatic statements in this introduction relating
to Paul's authority.

- "called an Apostle," 1 Cor. 1:1

- "by the will of God," 1 Cor. 1:1

- "by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ," 1 Cor. 1:10)

Paul's Apostolic authority is the major theological issue in the Corinthian letters, especially 2 Corinthians.

This same introductory phrase is used in Col. 1:1; 1 Cor. 1:1; 2 Cor. 1:1; and 2 Tim. 1:1. Paul
was convinced that God had chosen him to be an Apostle to the Gentiles. This special sense of calling began at his
Damascus road conversion (cf. Acts 9:1-22; 22:3-16; 26:9-18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WILL (thelēma) OF GOD

▣ "Sosthenes" This was possibly the Jewish leader mentioned in Acts 18:17, who was beaten by the mob
and possibly later became a believer and a local church leader. It is possible that he was Paul's

- helper

- scribe

- source of information about the church or

- someone the church knew well

However, all of this is speculation. We know so little about many of the people named in the NT.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 1 CORINTHIANS 1:2

2To the church of God which is at Corinth,
to those who have been sanctified in Christ Jesus, saints by calling, with all who in every place
call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:

1:2 "to the church" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

▣ "of God which is at Corinth" This phrase expresses two distinct senses about "the church."

- It is a local body of born again, baptized believers. Most of the places in the NT that the word
ekklesia is used reflect this local sense.

- It is also the universal expression of the Body of Christ.

- Matt. 16:18 (i.e., the first rare usage of this term by Jesus, cf. Matt. 18:17 [twice])

- Acts 9:31 uses the singular "church" for all the local congregations in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria

- the use of the term in Ephesians, which is a cyclical letter to the churches of western Asia Minor
(cf. Eph. 1:22; 3:10,21; 5:23-32).

There is one large Body of Christ made up of all believers (some now dead, some alive) and there are local
expressions of that universal body.

- the church victorious (believers with Jesus)

- the church militant (believers waiting for Jesus to return)

▣ "to those who have been sanctified" This is a PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE which means they
have been and continue to be declared holy by the work of Jesus through the agency of the Spirit (cf. 1 Cor. 6:11).
This term (hagiazō) is related to the word "holy" (hagios) and "saints" (i.e., "holy ones" hagioi).
It speaks of our separation to God for service. Here it refers to our position in Him as 1 Cor. 1:3 does, but other places
in the NT believers are to strive toward "holiness" (e.g., Matt. 5:48). It is a position to be possessed. Paul encourages
this factious, prideful church by calling them "saints" even amidst their failures and sins!

SPECIAL TOPIC: NT HOLINESS/SANCTIFICATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY ONES

▣ "in Christ Jesus" This grammatical form is designated as a LOCATIVE OF SPHERE. Believers are
sanctified

- by the Father (cf. 1 Thess. 5:23, i.e., the source, cf. John 17:7)

- through Jesus (i.e., the grounds, cf. 1 Cor. 1:2; Eph. 5:26)

- both aspects come together in Heb. 2:11

- it is normally the Holy Spirit to which this is attributed (i.e., the agency, cf. Rom. 15:16; 2 Thess. 2:13)

This is Paul's favorite way to designate believers. A good example of this is Eph. 1:3,4,7,9,10,12,13.
See William Barclay, The Mind of St. Paul, pp. 121-132. It means vital, personal union with Jesus (cf. Acts 17:28).

It is interesting to note how scribes sometimes have

- "in Christ Jesus" ‒ MSS P46, B, D, F, G

- "in Jesus Christ" ‒ MSS א, A

These kinds of variations occur often in the translation process of reading and copying. They do not affect the meaning,
but do show that the early scribes were more concerned with the basic meaning of a text and not rigid literalism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

▣ "by calling" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE PARTICIPLE. As Paul was called an Apostle,
so too, the Corinthian Christians were called saints (cf. Rom. 1:7). Notice the heavy emphasis on the doctrine
of election in this chapter in 1 Cor. 1:9,24,26,27,28. This construction refers to

- the initial act of God calling them

- their subsequent calling on Jesus in prayer for salvation

- which resulted in ongoing prayer, worship, and obedience

- Salvation is both an initial faith/repentance response and a continuing faith/repentance response.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

▣ "saints" "Saints" (hagioi) is theologically related to the OT term "holy,"
(kadosh) which means "set apart for God's service" (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY, cf. 1 Cor. 1:2; 2 Cor. 1:1; Rom. 1:1; Phil. 1:1; Col. 1:2). It is always PLURAL in
the NT except for one time in Philippians (4:21), but even there, it is used corporately. To be saved is to be part of the covenant
community of faith, the family of believers, the Body of Christ.

God's people are holy because of the imputed righteousness of Jesus (cf. Romans 4;
2 Cor. 5:21; Galatians 3). It is God's will that they live holy lives (cf. Lev. 11:44,45; 19:2; 20:7,26; Deut. 18:13;
Matt. 5:48; 1 Cor. 1:4; 4:1; 5:27; Col. 1:22; 3:12; 1 Pet. 1:16). Believers are both declared holy (positional sanctification)
and called to lifestyle holiness (progressive sanctification). Justification and sanctification must be affirmed together!
They must never be separated either doctrinally or practically.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SAINTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE

▣ "with all who in every place" Paul uses this phrase to remind the Corinthian believers that
they are part of a larger church family. They do not have the right to uniqueness or special treatment.
They must conform to the whole Body of Christ in doctrine and practice (cf. 1 Cor. 4:17; 7:17; 11:16; 14:33).

"To be sure, the relationship of faith and knowledge, pistis and gnosis, just
as that of faith and works, is ambivalent. On the one hand knowledge stands in faith's way, that is, when,
just as good works for the Jews, it represents the human will to self-redemption. As this antithesis is
developed in Galatians and Romans with respect to works, this threat to the Christian faith from the

danger exists not merely from the side of what Paul calls "the wisdom of this world" (1 Cor. 1:21), but
also from a certain kind of Christian gnosis. Paul does recognize that gnosis in itself: we
know that we all have knowledge (1 Cor. 8:1). But he immediately adds to this: knowledge puffs up, love
builds up. What is at issue here is a wrongly employed Christian gnosis, which elevates itself
above one's neighbor, the weak; a knowledge that is indeed in the service of one's own individual freedom,
but not of the edification of the church. This gnosis only promotes proud individualism and stands
over against love. In that sense gnosis, even as works, can come to stand over against love; as
such it is injurious and without profit (1 Cor. 13:2,3)" p. 242.
